findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated at import time, not per instance
findings.body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, not when each AssignmentSource instance is created. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (including via `from_integration`) will share the same import-time timestamp, making the field useless for tracking when a source was actually queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: `to_dict()` includes a datetime object that Celery's JSON serializer cannot handle
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` calls `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` datetime object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` then passes this dict to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. Celery's default JSON serializer cannot serialize datetime objects, so any inbound assignment/deassignment from an integration (where `assignment_source` is set) will raise a serialization error when enqueuing the outbound sync task, breaking the feature in production. The test suite likely does not catch this because tasks are executed synchronously in tests without going through Celery's serializer. The timestamp must be converted to a string (e.g., ISO format) or removed from the serialized dict.

findings.title: Unconditionally passing `assignment_source` to `sync_assignee_outbound` may break existing integrations
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` even when `parsed_assignment_source` is `None`. The abstract method signature in `IssueSyncIntegration` includes `**kwargs`, but concrete integration implementations may not accept an `assignment_source` keyword argument. Previously this kwarg was not passed, so adding it unconditionally can raise `TypeError` for integrations that do not define `**kwargs`. This is an API/contract break for third-party or existing integrations. Consider only passing the kwarg when it is not None, or ensuring all implementations accept **kwargs.

findings.title: No test verifies that outbound sync still occurs for a different integration
findings.body: The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only asserts that `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called when the source integration matches the target. It does not test that a different integration still receives the outbound sync. The PR's stated goal is to prevent cycles while still allowing other integrations to propagate changes, so a test covering the positive case for a non-matching integration would be valuable to prevent regressions where the filter becomes too broad.
